acceptance: A unit test fails if any Polars code path in benchbox/platforms/dataframe/ calls .collect( outside the single helper (static scan or monkeypatched LazyFrame.collect counting engine arguments)

A test proves engine=in-memory reaches scalar(), get_row_count() and unified-frame collects (for example by patching LazyFrame.collect and asserting the engine keyword on every call during TPC-H Q11, Q15 and Q22 at SF 0.01)

Result bundles carry requested engine, effective engine, polars version and polars-runtime-32 version (or an explicit absent marker); a fixture test covers both a pre-1.35 and a post-1.35 package layout
Requesting an unsupported engine value fails the run with an error naming the version and value
With no engine option, run output and bundle fields other than the new metadata are unchanged on 1.44.2; existing CI is green
context: Evidence (HEAD d076a974d): polars_df.py:372-374 collect() uses engine="streaming" when self.streaming, otherwise bare collect(); polars_df.py:406-408 scalar() does df.collect() when lazy; tpch/dataframe_queries.py:829, 863 and 1092 call ctx.scalar. Explorer _driver_version (transformer.py:374) prefers driver_version_actual for non-DuckDB platforms.
description:
The version matrix compares three engine setups: (A) each version's default collect(), which is in-memory on 1.x and streaming on 2.0; (B) in-memory on every version, which means engine="in-memory" on 2.0; (C) engine="streaming" where supported. That only works if one setting controls every materialization, and today it does not: PolarsDataFrameAdapter.scalar() calls a bare df.collect() (polars_df.py:408), and TPC-H Q11, Q15 and Q22 and several TPC-DS queries use ctx.scalar. get_row_count (polars_df.py:388), the path at polars_df.py:462, and 12 call sites in unified_frame.py also collect directly. As it stands, setup B would still run those inner steps streaming on 2.0.

Work:
- Add a polars-df platform option `engine` with values default, in-memory and streaming. `default` calls collect() with no engine argument, so each version uses its own default.
- Route every Polars materialization through one adapter helper that applies the option.
- Fold the existing streaming flag and engine_affinity tuning into the same helper without changing their current behaviour.
- Record in the result bundle the requested engine, the engine actually passed to collect, the polars version, and the polars-runtime-32 version when that package is installed (it exists from 1.35.2).

Guardrails:
- Default behaviour is unchanged: with no option set, the calls made must equal today's on the locked version.
- If a version does not support the requested engine value, fail the run with a clear error. Never fall back silently.
- No version-string branching, apart from detecting whether the `engine` keyword is accepted, if that proves necessary; document it if used.
